findings.source_quote: si credideritis ergo et audieritis verba mea et ambulaveritis in his et correxeritis itinera vestra, vivere poteritis.
findings.english_quote: Believe and listen to my words. Follow them and correct your ways. Then you will be able to live.
findings.issue: The source explicitly makes belief, hearing, walking and correcting one's ways the conditions of being able to live. The simplified edition replaces that conditional construction with independent imperatives followed by a consequence. Although the ethical content remains, the grammatical force of the shepherd's statement changes.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore an explicit condition while retaining accessible wording, for example: “So if you believe, listen to my words, follow them and correct your ways, you will be able to live.” This proposed wording requires fresh review.

findings.issue: The simplified edition omits the explicit emphasis of ipse, which identifies the shepherd himself as the speaker. Speaker identity remains correct, but this preserved emphasis is absent.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “The shepherd himself asked me,” subject to fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Haec omnia quae supra scripta sunt, ego pastor nuntius paenitentiae ostendi et locutus sum Dei servis.
findings.english_quote: Shorter sentences preserve the shepherd’s authority, ethical scope, blood-guilt and remedy language, and all noted alternatives.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims preservation of blood-guilt language, but this selected unit contains no blood-guilt assertion. This is an inaccurate description of the source and adaptation, even though blood-guilt has not been inserted into the reader text.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the blood-guilt claim and describe only features actually present in this unit, such as the shepherd's authority, the conditions for life, wholehearted repentance and the erasure of former sins. Review the replacement metadata independently.

summary: Both editions were reviewed clause by clause against the supplied Latin, with the disclosed bounded singular reading considered separately rather than silently replaced by the Latin plural. The standard edition is acceptable within this review's scope. The simplified edition needs correction of its conditional construction, omitted speaker emphasis and inaccurate blood-guilt metadata. Both preserve the adverse life assertion, negation, wholehearted repentance and the Lord's assessment without adding doctrinal conditions. Acceptance does not authenticate the reported Greek witnesses, unseen images, edition transcription or an exhaustive collation; proposed corrections require fresh review.
